content.text: Rught now, we want to start by essentially referring to Pokemon Red's harness, and build our own/modify our own. https://github.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon That would be first step. Now, we need to break it even further down into what is the subgoals we can see and how we can achieve it and verify it.
I’ll first map the reference harness against this repository, then turn that into small, independently verifiable milestones.

I found this checkout currently contains only an existing harness-planning document (plus untracked agent metadata), so I’m treating this as a discovery-and-plan step rather than assuming an implementation scaffold exists. I’m using the planning workflow to define explicit completion gates before any code is added.

Treat Pokémon Red as the architectural reference, not code to blindly port: its core boundary is “read memory → expose legal semantic choices → model chooses → harness presses buttons,” with no game-memory writes. [Reference README](https://github.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon) · [emulator wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon/main/src/emu/emulator.ts) · [state reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon/main/src/game/state.ts)

The first vertical slice should be narrow:

> From a known Emerald checkpoint at Birch’s starter choice, choose a starter, complete the forced battle using only legal model-selected actions, and produce a replayable evidence log.

| Subgoal | Build | Verify |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Prove emulator choice | Tiny mGBA Lua bridge spike: step frames, read RAM, press keys, save/load | One command advances frames, reads a known byte, and restores an identical save state |
| 1. Pin the target ROM | `RomProfile` with SHA-256, version, symbols, and explicit rejection | Known US Emerald v1.0 accepted; altered/unknown ROM rejected |
| 2. Make a reproducible start | User-local Birch checkpoint plus manifest/fingerprint | Load always reaches the same map, script state, and decision screen |
| 3. Establish the adapter contract | `EmulatorAdapter`: frame, buttons, RAM read, screenshot, save/load | Fake-adapter contract tests pass before using a real ROM |
| 4. Observe, don’t decide | Raw observation and typed decoder for party, battle, script/menu/cursor state | Fixture RAM snapshots decode to expected typed state |
| 5. Detect the decision branch | Classifier for starter selection, battle-menu input, busy text, and unsupported states | Recorded snapshots map to exactly one branch or an explicit “unsupported” result |
| 6. Generate legal semantic actions | `chooseStarter(Treecko|Torchic|Mudkip)` and only currently usable battle actions | No unavailable move, fainted switch, or invalid cursor position is emitted |
| 7. Compile and verify inputs | Cursor-relative button sequences and transition checks | Each action produces the intended cursor/party/battle-state transition; failure is logged |
| 8. Add policy safely | Deterministic fake + recorded-response policy before a live model client | Invalid response falls back safely; replay is deterministic |
| 9. Run the end-to-end proof | Start checkpoint → starter → battle → victory | Evidence JSONL contains profile ID, observation, legal options, chosen action, buttons, and verified outcome |
| 10. Harden after proof | Loop limits, checkpoint recovery, screenshots on failure, CI replay test | A deliberately bad response and a stalled state fail clearly, without silently progressing |

The current repo’s [existing plan](/home/kennc/Document/Github/PokemonEmerald/EMERALD_JEV_HARNESS_PLAN.md:1) already points at this same first proof, but it jumps straight to an mGBA/Python design. I would keep that as a hypothesis until Subgoal 0 proves the exact scripting and save-state capabilities needed; that prevents the emulator choice becoming an expensive constraint.

Planning record:

- Claim: build a minimal, ROM-safe Emerald harness whose first demonstrated capability is a replayable Birch-to-first-battle victory.
- Done-gate: real local-ROM run plus deterministic recorded replay, both ending with verified victory and complete JSONL.
- Base: `main` at `eaacc8c`; the plan document was introduced in that initial commit.
- Invariants: ROM-profile isolation; read-only game telemetry; semantic choices only; verified state transitions; explicit failures.
- Unknowns: exact Emerald RAM symbols for the chosen ROM revision, mGBA Lua API behavior, and whether a stable Birch checkpoint can be shared as a user-local recipe.

The subagent completed its read-only mGBA bridge investigation and is ready to return findings, but the collaboration wait mechanism failed before I could receive its final report.

Error verbatim:

```text
repeat-error-stop: the same error has now occurred 3 times in this session:
    {"message":"Wait timed out.\n\nRequested timeout of 1280ms was clamped to the minimum of 10000ms.","timed_out":true}
Do not re-run it.
```

I tried the wait mechanism with valid 30-second intervals after the initial clamped timeout; the final wait was blocked by this guard. This rules out an ordinary pending-agent delay, but not the subagent’s research itself—it reported that its investigation was complete.
I’m retrieving the completed investigator’s evidence now and will give you the concrete bridge feasibility result, not another planning layer.

End result: **mGBA is viable for our Emerald harness.** It can run headlessly with Lua, step exactly one video frame, read GBA RAM, set/release controller buttons, capture PNGs, and save/load states.

So the bridge can be:

```text
Python controller ⇄ local TCP ⇄ mGBA headless + Lua
                         │
               runFrame / RAM / keys / state
```

Important constraints:

- Use `emu:runFrame()` as the deterministic timing primitive.
- Read Emerald telemetry from EWRAM (`0x02000000…`) with `readRange`; keep it read-only.
- Button commands must specify press and release frame counts.
- Save-state loading defaults to excluding battery-save data, so checkpoint semantics must be tested with explicit flags.
- Python should connect to a Lua listener; Lua’s outbound connect blocks.
- The startup probe must verify scripting, Lua, PNG/VFS support, because packaged mGBA builds may omit them.

There is **no existing bridge implementation** in this repository yet—only the proposed design in [EMERALD_JEV_HARNESS_PLAN.md](/home/kennc/Document/Github/PokemonEmerald/EMERALD_JEV_HARNESS_PLAN.md:1).

The immediate next deliverable should therefore be a tiny bridge probe, not the full harness: launch mGBA headlessly, load a legal local Emerald ROM/state, answer five commands (`frame`, `readRange`, `keys`, `save`, `load`), and prove each with a pass/fail result. mGBA’s documented APIs support this shape: [scripting docs](https://mgba.io/docs/scripting.html), [headless script loading](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba/blob/1d201b22a86d31dfb3bc75145403711f6762015f/src/platform/headless-main.c#L195-L213).
